From: Elena Cortez <elena.cortez@museai.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing request: MuseAI assistant - dedicated GPU sizing

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this — MuseAI is evaluating a Dedicated pool for our conversational assistant (customer-facing, multi-tenant but we can isolate). We're trying to get an early understanding of committed GPU footprint before the execs sign off. High-level: ~2M active unique users/month, peak concurrency target around 4k sessions, prompt/response lengths vary by flow.

Attached is our quick sample traffic export (museai_sample_traffic.csv). Can Redwood fill the sizing template and give a ballpark (N gpus of type X for p99 latency < 300ms)? Also list the inputs you need if that sample isn't enough.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Cortez
Head of Infrastructure, MuseAI
elena.cortez@museai.com

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing request: MuseAI assistant - dedicated GPU sizing

Elena — thanks for the dataset. Looping in Marissa (pre-sales sizing lead).

We can definitely do a draft fitment. Quick ask: can you confirm the following fields (I attached our short sizer template):
- Prompt mix (percent of short prompts < 64 tokens, medium 64-256, long >256)
- Average response length per flow (tokens) and which flows are latency-sensitive
- Session vs stateless patterns (do you hold KV-cache per session?)
- Desired p50/p95/p99 tail targets and whether p99 is allowed to be higher on long responses

If you don't have everything, send what you can and we'll note assumptions. I'll attach redwood_sizer_template.xlsx for quick fill.

Kimberly Park
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Cortez <elena.cortez@museai.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing request: MuseAI assistant - dedicated GPU sizing

Elena — quick technical clarifications from the sizing side (so our numbers aren't off):
1) KV cache/sessionization: If you pin a KV cache per session it increases memory pressure and reduces packing; we need session TTL (average minutes) and expected concurrent sessions (not just API concurrency).
2) Prompt/response distribution: please give percent of requests that include context >2k tokens (e.g., agent handoff, long context search). Those blow up compute for a single token step.
3) RLHF/streaming vs batch responses: do you stream tokens to the client? For streaming we target different batching heuristics.
4) Prompt engineering: are you running multiple model calls per user request (e.g., rerank + generate)? If yes, pipeline the calls and give counts per request.

Tentative assumptions I will use unless you correct them:
- Prompt mix: 60% short, 35% medium, 5% long
- Avg response tokens: 40/180/650 respectively
- Session TTL: 15 minutes, average concurrent sessions = 60% of API concurrency
- 1.1 model calls per user (small percent of requests include a rerank)

I'll sketch a sizing matrix (gpu types, concurrency per GPU, p99 tail) and share a ballpark.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Pre-sales Capacity Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Elena Cortez <elena.cortez@museai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing request: MuseAI assistant - dedicated GPU sizing

Marissa/Kim — thanks, answers inline and attached a short prompt mix doc (museai_prompt_mix.md):
- KV cache: yes, we use session affinity with per-session KV stored in memory; TTL ~20 minutes; expecting sessions ~= 55% of API concurrency during peak.
- Long context (>2k tokens): ~2% of requests (search/knowledge-heavy flows).
- Streaming: yes for chat flows (clients prefer token streaming).
- Multi-call: ~1.2 calls/request on average (embedding + generate for some workflows).

Attached: museai_prompt_mix.md and updated sample traffic (same CSV, added flow tags). Can you give a ballpark GPU count and which GPU SKUs you'd recommend for p99 < 300ms for short/medium flows? We're flexible on model flavor but want to optimize cost for production.

Elena

Attachments: museai_prompt_mix.md (md), museai_sample_traffic.csv (csv)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Cortez <elena.cortez@museai.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sizing request: MuseAI assistant - dedicated GPU sizing

Elena — thanks for the detail, this is enough for a first-pass. High level ballpark (assumptions noted):
Assumptions we used: 4k peak concurrent API requests, prompt mix per Marissa's defaults updated with your 2% long-context, session-affinity TTL 20m, 1.2 calls/request, streaming enabled. Using Llama-3-like 13B quantized runtime as a cost/latency target:
- Short/medium p99 < 300ms: ~8-12 A10G-equivalent GPUs for sustained peak (depends on exact batching and KV cache overhead).
- If you want stronger headroom for long-context steps (2% heavy), add 2-3 additional A100-40G-class GPUs or route long-context flows to slower offline workers to reduce cost.
- If you choose a smaller 7B quantized model across the fleet, converse p99 for short flows can be satisfied with ~5-7 A10G-equivalents.

Next steps I propose:
1) Short 30m call with our sizing team to review the CSV and walk through peak-minute examples (I can run a quick session-concurrency sim).
2) If you can upload a tokenized sample of heavy flows we can run a micro-bench to tighten the numbers.

Suggested times (PDT): Thu 08/14 10:00 or Thu 08/14 15:00.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
